problems.comment:
The avalanche danger will increase during the day. As a consequence of new snow and a strong to storm force westerly wind, wind slabs will form. These will be deposited on a weakly bonded old snowpack on shady slopes above approximately 2600 m. Avalanches can in some places be released by a single winter sport participant and reach medium size. 
 Backcountry touring calls for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger.

bulletin.snowpack: There is still only a little snow. As a result of the rain, the thin old snowpack became moist up to high altitude. This is a rather favourable base for the new and wind-drifted snow from Wednesday.
bulletin.tendency: The danger of dry avalanches will increase slightly. Even single winter sport participants can release avalanches, including in deeper layers. Backcountry touring and other off-piste activities call for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger and caution.

problems.comment:
As a consequence of new snow and a strong to storm force westerly wind, sometimes avalanche prone wind slabs will form. The new snow and wind slabs are lying on top of a weakly bonded old snowpack in particular on steep shady slopes above approximately 2600 m. 
 Avalanches can be released by a single winter sport participant. Mostly they are medium-sized. Natural avalanches are possible as the day progresses. 
 Backcountry touring calls for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger.

bulletin.snowpack:
With rain and occasional thunderstorms, the snowpack became moist locally as high as 3000 m and thoroughly wet at lower altitudes.
With a lot of new snow and a continuing storm-force westerly wind, additional wind slabs are forming, mostly in areas distant from ridgelines. Avalanches can be triggered within the various layers of new and wind-drifted snow. On high-altitude shady slopes, avalanches can also be triggered in coarse-grained weak layers of the old snowpack.
bulletin.tendency: As a consequence of new snow and strong wind there will be an additional increase in the avalanche danger to level 4 (high). The danger exists in particular in alpine snow sports terrain. Numerous medium-sized and large natural avalanches are to be expected. Transportation routes situated at higher altitudes can be endangered occasionally. The conditions are very critical for snow sport activities outside marked and open pistes.

problems.comment:
As a consequence of new snow and a strong to storm force westerly wind, large wind slabs will form. Avalanches can be released by a single winter sport participant. 
 The avalanche danger will increase but remain within the current danger level. An increasing number of natural avalanches are to be expected as the day progresses. In particular on steep shady slopes they can be released in the weakly bonded old snow and reach large size, in particular above approximately 2600 m. 
 Backcountry touring calls for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger and caution.
